A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLIM research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-U. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment; differences are confined to pages 1, 9, and 10.

before.justification: v3 reports original compression experiments, including downstream accuracy in Tables 1-3, WikiText-2 perplexity in Appendix G, GPU speed measurements, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original accuracy, perplexity, speed, and sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-2 retain identical quantization, pruning, saliency-based adapter construction, adapter quantization, and optional fine-tuning procedures.

E1.justification: The six downstream tasks, WikiText-2 evaluations, and C4 and SlimPajama data usage are unchanged. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding main-text and appendix tables retain identical comparator membership, including SparseGPT, Wanda, JSQ, L2QER, and MaskLLM in their respective experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and the appendices retain the same metrics, model configurations, calibration sample counts, quantization settings, and fine-tuning protocols. The added report link introduces no experimental setting.

E4.justification: Component comparisons and supplementary analyses are unchanged, including input quantization, weight versus output error minimization, and the rank, calibration, and sparsity sensitivity studies in Appendices O-R.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the reported performance.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical throughout the main text and appendices. The new external-report link adds no per-task result values within v4.pdf.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13, the quantization formulation, saliency assumptions, and mathematical analyses in Appendices L, M, and O are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about one-shot compression, accuracy, speed, memory reduction, and optional fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Result interpretations, computational trade-offs, applicability qualifications, and limitations remain identical, including Appendix T's disclosure that fine-tuning hyperparameters were not tuned.

D1.justification: At the end of Section 4, v4 adds a Weights & Biases report link for per-task downstream accuracy details. This adds access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, and the existing code/data link are unchanged. The report's contents are outside the supplied evidence.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, introduction's research positioning, and Appendix S related-work discussion are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds the report-link sentence, adds Ray Hung to the acknowledgments, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence slightly reflows page 9, reduces spacing below Figure 2, and shifts the conclusion downward. The acknowledgments rewrap on page 10. Figures, captions, tables, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new Section 4 link provides an explicit location for inspecting per-task accuracy details, offering a modest documentation benefit. Scientific content and appendix evidence remain unchanged. This assessment credits the added access guidance; the external report's contents cannot be assessed from the supplied PDFs.
